newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply off as locals, trade sell.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply off as locals, trade sell.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures retraced recent gains to close sharply weaker amid local and trade selling and with a lack of follow-through buying, dealers said.
Analysts had predicted a retracement of recent gains as the market climbed to seven-week highs in the face of bearish fundamentals.

"We had a few consecutive days of up-peaks but didn't have the fundamentals supporting the rally," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said. "The market became overbought and now it's retracing."
Market analysts forecast further weakness as supplies continue to grow and demand for juice remains tepid. Nearby support was pegged at today's low of 82.00 cents in July.
Resistance was seen at Monday's high of 86.75 cents and then at 87.45 cents, the high reached on March 25.

The July contract closed down 3.05 cents at 82.65 cents per lb, having ranged from 85.60 to 82.00 cents. Second-position September finished 2.95 lower at 84.70 cents, while the rest of the board closed 2.65 and 2.60 lower.
An estimated 3,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Monday's official 4,227 lots.
